items.title: MIIT issues rules for AI-agent devices: phones with preinstalled agents need adaptation and anti-fraud checks to get network access
items.original_title: 工信部：加强智能体终端设备进网管理
items.summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology issued a notice (工信厅信管〔2026〕42号) on 6 Nov governing 'agent terminals', meaning phones, tablets and wearables with preinstalled AI agents. Such devices must pass adaptation verification plus fraud-risk and anti-fraud capability evaluation during network-access testing, and agents should carry a unique identity code under the national agent-interconnect standards. Over-the-air agent upgrades require an upgrade plan filed with MIIT and a report afterwards. App-distribution platforms must have developers declare by e-signature whether agents may call their apps, and agents that have not been declared consented to may not force-call apps.
items.why_it_matters: It writes into regulation the dispute behind ByteDance's Doubao phone assistant and the app-refusal lists: third-party apps get a formal consent mechanism, and every agent phone faces a pre-sale regulatory gate.

learn.title: Report a monitor's recall at a fixed false-accusation rate, with an interval
learn.why_today: The Project EVE item reports monitor agents catching 30-40% of saboteurs at 5% false accusations, a recall-at-fixed-FPR number.
learn.explanation: A monitor outputs a score; a single accuracy figure hides the trade-off between catching saboteurs and accusing honest agents. Fix the false-positive rate first (here 5%), set the threshold at the matching quantile of honest-agent scores, then report recall (true-positive rate) at that threshold. With only tens of positives the estimate is noisy, so bootstrap the saboteur scores to get an interval. It breaks when honest scores are not representative of deployment, or when saboteurs adapt to the threshold. The numbers below are illustrative, not from the Anthropic study.

import random
random.seed(0)
# Illustrative: a monitor scores agents; saboteurs score higher on average.
n_s, n_h = 40, 400
sab = [random.gauss(1.5, 1.0) for _ in range(n_s)]
hon = [random.gauss(0.0, 1.0) for _ in range(n_h)]
# threshold = (1 - FPR) quantile of honest scores
fpr = 0.05
thr = sorted(hon)[int((1 - fpr) * n_h)]
tp = sum(s > thr for s in sab)
recall = tp / n_s
def boot():
    r = [random.choice(sab) for _ in range(n_s)]
    return sum(s > thr for s in r) / n_s
bs = sorted(boot() for _ in range(2000))
print(f"threshold={thr:.2f} recall@5%FPR={recall:.2f} 95% CI=({bs[50]:.2f},{bs[1949]:.2f})")
